title: [core][misc] improve free_finished_seq_groups

experiments.name: free_finished_seq_groups_throughput
experiments.workload: facebook/opt-125m offline batch, benchmark_throughput.py input-len 16 output-len 16 num-prompts 100000; scheduler's free_finished_seq_groups is on the critical path every model step.
experiments.note: Diff rewrites free_finished_seq_groups (scheduler.py) to scan only the running deque instead of iterating running+swapped+waiting every step, so finished-request detection no longer walks the full 100k-prompt backlog. Number source: PR body opt-125m 100k-prompt throughput 211.18 -> 522.91 req/s (slowdown vs 10k cut to ~40%).

reported.scope: full offline-batch serving throughput with 100k pending prompts on a tiny model where scheduler overhead dominates, not the isolated free_finished_seq_groups call
reported.scale_short: Author's req/s is whole-engine offline-batch throughput with a 100k-prompt backlog; the diff speeds up one scheduler scan. TO MAKE 1:1: microbench free_finished_seq_groups alone with a large running+waiting queue, old full-queue scan vs running-only scan.
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (req/s) but 211.18 -> 522.91 is end-to-end benchmark_throughput on opt-125m with 100k prompts, where the scheduler's per-step full-queue scan dominated; on small backlogs the gain vanishes. The headline '40%' is the reduced slowdown going 10k->100k prompts, not a flat per-call ratio. Direction genuine; magnitude is backlog-size dependent.

environment: reported-only: author's published numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
